cells.tense: The work is finished and set down, and the body has not braced at all.
cells.act: keep the connection coherent while it is hard
cells.ask: Hand a finished piece over whole and stay while the receiving is awkward. Let the unease sit in your body and keep the thread intact between you two.
cells.core:
You finish things, and you finish them in a way that holds — whatever you build still stands after you've walked away from it. What you can do right now is finish and stay: hand a thing over while it's still fresh, and be present when the reception isn't clean. That's the harder part of completing something, and you're standing in the middle of it.

Hand a finished piece over whole and stay with whoever takes it while the receiving is awkward. Don't smooth the ending. Nothing needs repair before they see it. What you'll have is a completion the other person was actually part of, which no solo finish can give you.
cells.sheetLine: You finish things. Now finish one where someone can see.
cells.verb: Building the thing to last, and knowing when the last thing is done
cells.place: The threshold where a finished work is carried out and set down whole

cells.tense: You will have decided what everything becomes before any of it has arrived.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: Set something you're building beside another person's side of it — what it asks of them against what it hands them — and let their weight count as much as yours before you settle it.
cells.core:
You can build, and build past the point anyone is standing there. Somewhere in the bracing a structure is going up for people who haven't been asked what they'll carry, and the strength that's supposed to hold things is arriving ahead of everything it's meant to hold.

Set something you're building beside another person's side of it — what it asks of them against what it hands them — and let their weight count the same as yours. You don't have to fix the outcome or agree with them. You're letting the scale hold both ends at once, and what you build after that can be stood in by whoever wasn't consulted at the start.
cells.sheetLine: You're building walls people haven't been asked to carry.
cells.verb: Building the thing to last, and knowing when the last thing is done

cells.tense: You finished it already and you are still holding it as though it were alive.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Pick a finished thing you're still carrying and close it cleanly in your own space, then go forward carrying only the part that isn't done.
cells.core:
Carrying a finished thing out and setting it down whole, hands empty, ready for what's next — that's the shape you're built for, and the body knows the difference between a live work and a closed one. It moves on without being told. That part's still yours.

Your hands are still on the scaffold after the building stopped. Pick a finished thing you're still carrying. Close it cleanly in your own space — no announcement, no one to tell — and go forward carrying only the part that isn't done. Letting go isn't the opposite of building. It's the last act of building, and what remains will have your hands free for it.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it. Your hands are still on the scaffold.
cells.verb: Building the thing to last, and knowing when the last thing is done
cells.place: The threshold where a finished work is carried out and set down whole

cells.tense: The building is underway and the author has stepped off the scaffold.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a small new thing because beginning it feels good, and treat it as a beginning rather than a project with an end in sight.
cells.core:
You have been building the thing that holds your life together — the structure around your time, your work, the people close to you — and the story you tell is that it holds itself. It doesn't. It holds because someone keeps it standing, and that someone is you, present at the work.

Begin a small new thing because beginning it feels good, and treat it as a beginning rather than a project with an end in sight. Something you'd start because starting it is good, not because it will be solid. What you make this way belongs to you in a way your standing work has stopped feeling like, and you get to be inside the making while it's still new.
cells.sheetLine: The building holds because you're holding it. Say so.
cells.verb: Building the thing to last, and knowing when the last thing is done
cells.place: The threshold where a finished work is carried out and set down whole
